firstMismatch.message: Replay error: env is not defined

mismatch.message: Replay error: env is not defined

summary: When a touch-petrifying hero is engulfed by a non-stone-resistant monster, mhitu.c:gulpmu relocates the attacker to its original square and calls trap.c:minstapetrify before clearing the hero’s stuck link. The JavaScript call passes undeclared `env` from a function whose supplied environment is `rawEnv`, so replay stops at this branch before the C stoning, kill-credit, and release behavior.

source.branch: In gulpmu’s initial-swallow branch, after a successful engulf, when touch_petrifies(gy.youmonst.data) is true and resists_ston(mtmp) is false, restore the attacker to its pre-engulf square, call minstapetrify(mtmp, TRUE), restore a punished ball and chain if present, then clear u.ustuck and return the attack result.
callers: mhitu.c:mattacku dispatches AT_ENGL attacks to gulpmu; this v74 case reaches that production caller.
mhitu.c:gulp_blnd_check also calls gulpmu for the already-swallowed AD_BLND follow-up; it is an independent production caller.
dependencies: trap.c:minstapetrify is already implemented in js/trap.js; this correction only supplies gulpmu’s existing rawEnv to that helper.

evidence: The admitted C recording challenges/cases/v74/v74-cockatrice-trapper-engulf-action2.session.json has 230 input steps. C step 170 prints “The trapper folds itself around you!” and “The trapper is slowing down”; step 171 prints “The trapper turns to stone.” Prep’s unchanged-input prefix reaches the engulf transition at step 170.

nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:1289-1380 establishes the call preconditions and order: gulpmu moves the engulfer onto the hero, binds it, emits the engulf message, then checks touch_petrifies(gy.youmonst.data) && !resists_ston(mtmp); on that branch C restores the engulfer’s original coordinates and calls minstapetrify before placebc/set_ustuck(NULL).

nethack-c/upstream/include/monsters.h:990-998 defines the trapper as AT_ENGL/AD_WRAP with no MR_STONE. The recipe’s hero polymorphs into a cockatrice and creates a hostile trapper, so both sides of the C predicate are source-supported.

js/mhitu.js:2224 names the supplied callback object rawEnv; js/mhitu.js:2378 instead evaluates `env` at the minstapetrify call. That unresolved identifier throws before the existing js/trap.js:minstapetrify implementation can run. The branch then must preserve the existing source-order ball/chain restoration and set_ustuck cleanup.
